To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) spiders and solifugids have a fluid secretion that lubricates their adhesive contact zone, 2) this fluid secretion is not always present, 3) spider adhesive setae have lower static friction than gecko setae, and 4) this may be explained by fluid secretion.
spider and solifugid adhesive setae secrete a thin film of fluid that lubricates the contact zone.
“Spider adhesive pads secrete fluid over their adhesive pads, which lubricates the contact zone and improves adhesion to rough substrates.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adhesive mechanisms used by spiders, mites and other arachnids, and with the evolution of these mechanisms.
the adhesive properties of the feet of spiders and other arachnids, which is important for their survival in their natural habitats.
the question of how animals adhere to smooth, non-adhesive surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spider and gecko adhesive systems have converged on a similar hairy structure, which allows them to adhere to smooth surfaces by dry (solid–solid) intermolecular interaction, but the presence of fluid secretions in the contact zone of the spider adhesive pad is a key difference.
the spider adhesive pads are wet and the gecko adhesive pads are dry.
all arachnids have a fluid layer on the adhesive surface, and this fluid layer is secreted by the arachnid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spiders, solifuges and mites all have adhesive pads that are lubricated by secretions, and that the adhesive pads of geckos and the anole lizard Anolis carolinensis are dry.
the adhesive contact zones of all the terrestrial animals with adhesive pads we tested (spiders, solifugid and mites) leave behind a thin film of fluid on smooth surfaces.
spider adhesives are wetter than we thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of fluid in an adhesive contact has important consequences for performance.
the secreted fluid is not just a lubricant.
spiders and solifugids are wet adhesives.
